perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s available perspective:

- Harold is a project manager and has been feeling frustrated and anxious because he believes his project team is unmotivated and that this is hurting project progress.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer, friend/colleague, and someone he relies on for advice and support.
- Harold arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. He told Arthur that his team seemed completely unmotivated. He heard Arthur suggest understanding each team member’s individual motivations and having one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood.
- After that meeting, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He believed Arthur’s advice might help and decided to implement it.
- Harold told his team he wanted quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them and asked them to make the project a success together.
- After implementing the advice, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He spoke with Arthur again and told him the suggestions had not worked. He heard Arthur say there may be deeper issues—personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors—and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of one-on-one meetings to investigate.
- In those meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by workload and stressed, which made motivation hard.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks to ease pressure. He said their well-being was important to him.
- Harold then felt optimistic and empowered. He believed addressing individual concerns could improve team performance.
- He told the team he would create a more supportive and open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said their input and well-being were crucial and urged everyone to work together for project success.

He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, hidden motives, or narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or did himself.
